success_patterns: Three of the eight (Welsh, Rhapsody, Grasshopper pie) had the clue echoed in a flashcard or trivia-archive passage, with the answer attached or recoverable from the other passages. The agent copied the repeated entity, which Rule 3 already covers.
For a 'this <type>' clue the agent answered with the entity of that type (language, constellation, ethnic group, film, book, person) and not with an anchor word from the clue.
The agent ignored joke asides ('looks nothing like Kevin Sorbo') for the core answer, but the aside was in fact a corroborating hint (the actor's famous role, Hercules).
A fractional or approximate quantity in the clue ('about 1/5 the population') was matched to the passages' own figure ('21 percent') to select among several candidate groups.
A dish name kept its head noun ('Grasshopper pie') when the clue described the modifier only indirectly ('insect name', 'green'), so the bare modifier would not name the dish.

patch.reasoning: Most of this batch is already handled by existing rules (archive hits, type slot, bare short answers). Three small gaps showed up. First, numeric paraphrase matching (1/5 -> 21%) is not stated anywhere and is a common way to disambiguate between several plausible entities. Second, the skill says jokes are pure decoration, yet the Kevin Sorbo aside was a real corroborating pointer to the answer. Third, the head-noun exception needs a food-dish example where the clue states the category noun ('pie') but not the modifier ('Grasshopper'), to balance the many 'drop the head noun' rules. All three are low-risk, carry no task-specific facts beyond one-line examples, and do not touch Rule 3's verbatim-override behavior or the protected block.

edits.target: ## Rule 3: Look for the clue repeated verbatim in the context
edits.content: - NUMERIC / FRACTION clues ('about 1/5 the population', 'nearly half', 'a third of the world's X'): convert the clue's quantity to the percentage or figure the passages use (1/5 = about 20%, here a passage saying '21 percent') and pick the candidate whose stated share fits. Reject candidates whose figures are clearly different (10%, 17%, 30%).

edits.target: are decoration. Answer from the factual core plus the anchor term.
edits.content: are mostly decoration. Answer from the factual core plus the anchor term. If an aside names a person or work tied to the answer (an actor's famous role, 'looks nothing like <actor>'), use it only as corroboration of the candidate your factual core already gives, never as the answer itself.

edits.target: ## Rule 4: Exact-match formatting of the final answer
edits.content: - FOOD / DISH names keep their head noun when the clue states the category noun but only hints at the modifier ('Southern pie with an insect name ... green, cookie-crumb crust' -> 'Grasshopper pie', since bare 'Grasshopper' does not name the dish). Drop the head noun only when the clue itself states the modifier ('A "hasty" dessert' -> 'pudding'). Copy the capitalization/wording used in the passages.
